notes: §1985:VI.3.3.2 prints the paragraph as the header PROGRAM-ID, a period, program-name and a period, nothing else; the only 1985 additions are the Inter-Program module's COMMON and INITIAL (§1985:X.3.1.2). The grammar rule programIdParagraph requires both periods and exactly one programName (a word, never a literal), and parses the later editions' tails as a superset that 1985 refuses by name: VersionConformancePass.VisitExternalizedNamePhrase refuses AS literal-1 (COBOL0900), VisitProgramIdAttributes refuses RECURSIVE (COBOL0885) and VisitPrototypePhrase refuses IS PROTOTYPE (COBOL0900), each a 2002 introduction; BinderDriver.MakeUnit takes the unit's name from the paragraph. The witness compiles and runs a program whose paragraph is PROGRAM-ID. PGMID1. Probed further at --std 85: the name on the line after the header, lower case, and a comma separator before the period are accepted, as is IS INITIAL PROGRAM; AS with a literal or a word, RECURSIVE with and without IS, IS PROTOTYPE, IS GLOBAL, IS PROGRAM with no attribute, a literal or an integer as the name, two names, no name, a missing period after the header or after the name, a second PROGRAM-ID paragraph, and the 1985 reserved words MOVE, ALTER, SECURITY and CD as the name are each refused.

next.reason: 1985: "PROGRAM-ID. program-name."; 2023: "PROGRAM-ID. program-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] [ IS ... RECURSIVE ... PROGRAM ] .". 2023 still accepts the 1985 form, but its format adds optional phrases (AS literal-1, RECURSIVE) that the 1985 format does not allow, so more programs are accepted.
